subject: Dedicated capacity: GPU mix & TPS profile follow-up — Iterative.ai evaluation
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@iterative.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 28 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated capacity: GPU mix & TPS profile follow-up — Iterative.ai evaluation

Thanks again for the call this morning — great context and helpful product walkthrough. This thread captures the follow-ups we discussed and the sizing info we need to propose a concrete Dedicated configuration. I also attached the TPS profile template (iterative_tps_profile.csv) you can drop your per-route trace into.

TL;DR (recommendation preview)
- Based on the mix you described: short prompts (~<100 tokens) dominate, but you have a non-trivial tail of long-context jobs (~700–2k tokens).
- We recommend a hybrid Dedicated pool: primarily cost-efficient L4/A10-style nodes for short prompts + 1–2 H100/A100 class nodes for long-context/large-batch workloads.

What I need from you (so we can produce an estimate):
1) Peak and 95th-percentile TPS by route (attached CSV). If you can, include time-of-day so we can size for burst capacity.
2) Token mix: percent short (<100 tokens), medium (100–512), long (>512). Example below.
3) Any latency SLOs (p99/p95) and whether tail latency >500ms is acceptable for long jobs.

Notes on tradeoffs we discussed:
- H100/A100: best for long-context and throughput-sensitive batching; lower cost-per-token for very long outputs but higher hourly footprint.
- A100/L4 (cost-efficient): great for sub-200-token low-latency traffic; can deliver sub-150ms p95 for short prompts when colocated and with KV caching.
- Continuous batching + prefix caching will help reduce unit costs for repeated prompt patterns.

Proposed next steps:
- You drop a 48-hour token trace into the attached CSV or paste a sample JSON (iterative_token_sample.json).
- We run a quick throughput simulation and send a Draft Dedicated SKU/estimate (I’ll include Marissa on pricing).
- Schedule a 60-minute sizing workshop (I’ll bring our infra lead) — proposed window: Mon Feb 1 or Tue Feb 2 (PST).

Attachments: iterative_tps_profile.csv (template)

Thanks —
Karthik
Karthik Iyer

Thanks Karthik — attaching a quick token breakdown and a short sample trace (iterative_token_sample.json). High-level answers below so you can start rough-sizing: 

- Token mix (approx): short (<100 tokens): 68% 
- medium (100–512): 20%
- long (>512): 12% (longs are mostly nightly batch runs and model-generated summaries)

Traffic profile (prod-ish):
- Steady baseline: ~22–30 QPS (us-east) across user-facing routes during business hours
- Peak burst windows (marketing campaigns / scheduled jobs): up to 170 QPS sustained for ~10–20 minutes, with infrequent spikes to ~220 QPS for <5 minutes
- Concurrency expectation: ~120 concurrent requests at peak (this maps to ~3–4k concurrent tokens in-flight depending on mix)

Latency SLOs: p95 user-facing <300ms for short prompts; long batch jobs can tolerate higher latency (p95 < 4s).

We definitely prefer Dedicated for latency predictability and data isolation. Private/VPC is a future requirement (6–12 months) but not immediate. Hosted API would not meet our compliance and data residency needs.

Let me know if the token sample is enough or if you need raw logs — we can export from our inference layer.

—Elena
Elena Ruiz
Head of ML Product, Iterative.ai
elena@iterative.ai

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 28 Jan 2027 13:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: GPU mix & TPS profile follow-up — Iterative.ai evaluation

Appreciate the fast turnaround and the trace — this is exactly what we need. Quick initial sizing thoughts (ballpark until we run the sim):

Sizing assumptions I’m using from your numbers:
- 70% short prompts, p95 target <300ms -> prioritize low-latency nodes
- 12% long prompts, p95 target <4s -> batch-friendly nodes for throughput
- Peak burst to 170–220 QPS for ~10–20min -> need buffer for autoscale/burst or a small reserved burst pool

Option A — Balanced (recommended starting point):
- 4 x L4-class nodes (low-latency pool) handling short prompts; each node ~ 45–55 QPS for sub-100 token avg with aggressive batching + KV cache.
- 2 x H100-class nodes (long-context pool) dedicated to batch/long jobs; each H100 can run large-batch pipelines with higher throughput for long tokens.
- Warm buffer: 1 small A100 instance to absorb spikes and for canary/fallback.

Option B — Latency-first (higher cost):
- 6 x L4-class nodes, 1 x H100. Best for p95 under 200ms most of the day; higher hourly spend.

Option C — Cost-optimized (more batching tolerance):
- 3 x L4, 1 x H100, rely on burst autoscale + queued requests for occasional spikes. Lower steady cost, higher tail latency during bursts.

Operational notes:
- We’ll enable continuous prefix/KV caching for repeated patterns (saves ~20–35% token cost on short prompt-heavy routes).
- For your peak windows we recommend a short reserved burst pool (2–3 instances) to avoid cold-scaling friction; Redwood can keep a hot buffer that only bills while reserved.

I’ve attached a draft estimate workbook (dedicated_estimate_q1_v2.xlsx) with rough hourly and per-token cost ranges per option — Marissa will confirm pricing/discounting in a minute.

Next concrete steps:
1) Run sim against iterative_token_sample.json and your CSV (I'll run this and return a throughput profile by EOD tomorrow).
2) 60-minute sizing workshop: Mon Feb 1 at 10:30 AM PST (confirmable).
3) If the sim matches, we’ll issue a POC SKU (3-month reserve + burst) you can trial.

On the privacy/VPC timeline — noted; we’ll include notes for the Private deployment path and what migration looks like.

-Karthik

Elena — looping in pricing. A couple of quick notes on commitments and burst: 

- For a POC we typically propose a 3-month reserved pool with the ability to scale burst for short windows. We can do a trial credit against the first month if you want to validate performance.
- If you commit to a 12-month reserved commitment we can provide a deeper discount and priority capacity during marketing-driven spikes.
- On region: US-east capacity availability is high for L4/A100; H100 inventory is more constrained but we can prioritize allocation if you signal intent.

I’ll attach the pricing worksheet after Karthik sends his sim results. Happy to take a call after the sizing workshop to lock in numbers.
